text:
Sam Lee: Hey — running into a weird local-compose problem after switching from Docker Desktop -> Colima. Postgres container keeps exiting with permission errors on /var/lib/postgresql/data (Postgres logs: "could not open file \"postmaster.pid\": Permission denied"). I had the data dir bind-mounted to a host path. Also, intermittently my dev app can't connect to Redis: it says ERR - NOAUTH but the container is configured with a password in compose. Any quick tips?

Priya N: welcome! two quick things: on mac with Colima the host mount ends up chowned to root inside the VM. prefer a named volume for PG if you can.

Priya N: If you must use a host mount, chown inside the VM (colima) to the postgres uid (usually 999).

Priya N: ```bash
# from your mac
colima ssh
sudo chown -R 999:999 /path/to/host/pgdata
exit
docker-compose up -d db
```

Devon: FWIW we avoid bind mounts for PG on dev machines for exactly this reason. named volume in compose is simplest:

Devon: ```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
volumes:
  pgdata: {}
```

Devon: that way the volume is managed inside the runtime and you won't hit host-perm surprises.

Alex M: Another trick if you need host mounts: set the service to run as the postgres uid in the container so files created are owned compatibly: `user: \"999:999\"` on the db service. Not ideal but works for local dev.

Priya N: For the Redis AUTH issue, verify redis actually picked the password. Exec into the container and run `redis-cli -a <pass> ping`. If that fails, maybe your env var is not injected into the redis service or you're accidentally running a different redis container locally. Healthchecks help.

Priya N: Example redis check:```bash
docker-compose exec redis redis-cli -a "$REDIS_PASSWORD" ping
# should reply PONG
```

infra-bot: dev-runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/local-db-setup — has Colima notes and common fixes :memo:

Sam Lee: Thanks! I tried `colima ssh` and chowned the host dir to 999/999 and postgres actually starts now. Quick followup — my init SQL that creates extensions (pgvector) runs during init and now errors out with "could not open extension control file". Could that be related to image mismatch?

Devon: Possibly — if you're using a slim image that doesn't have the extension package, it won't be present. Use the same image we use in dev (check the runbook) or install the extension in the image. For pgvector we use `postgres:15` + `apt-get install -y postgresql-15-pgvector` in our dev Dockerfile.

Sam Lee: OK will try switching to named volume + matching image + re-run compose. Really appreciate the help :thumbsup:

Alex M: If you re-use the host mount and keep hitting perms, drop the volume, then `docker-compose up -d` to re-init the DB once the ownership is fixed. If you want I can pair for 10m later.

Sam Lee: That would be awesome — pinging you in a bit. Thanks all!
